lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 92, which adds the -t and -T options to open folders as tabs in one new window.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request 92, which adds the dash t and dash capital T options to open folders as tabs in one new window.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
You run thunar with -t and some folders, then -T and more folders.
lines.say: You run Thunar with dash t and some folders, then dash capital T and more folders.

lines.caption: Still in your own process, the command splits its arguments at -T, and marks the right-pane folders.
lines.say: Still in your own process, the command splits its arguments at dash capital T, and marks the right-pane folders.

lines.caption: Then GApplication hands the options to the Thunar that is already running, over D-Bus.
lines.say: Then G Application hands the options to the Thunar that is already running, over D bus.

lines.caption: That Thunar reads the new options, and the list of right-pane folders.
It checks each folder in turn; a bad one gets the usual error dialog, and the rest still open.
It always opens a new window, as with -w, and skips restoring last session's tabs.
lines.say: It always opens a new window, as with dash w, and skips restoring last session's tabs.

lines.caption: A new window function fills the left pane, turns split view on only with -T, and fills the right pane.
lines.say: A new window function fills the left pane, turns split view on only with dash capital T, and fills the right pane.

lines.caption: Finally the first tab is selected in each pane, and the keyboard focus goes back to the left pane.
Until now each folder opened in its own window; there was no way to build a two-pane window of tabs in one command.
The key fact: the thunar you type usually just forwards its options to a running Thunar, so the split must happen first.
lines.say: The key fact: the Thunar you type usually just forwards its options to a running Thunar, so the split must happen first.

lines.caption: The split rewrites each folder after -T as a hidden option; -T with no folder prints an error, unless help is asked for.
lines.say: The split rewrites each folder after dash capital T as a hidden option; with no folder after it, it prints an error, unless help is asked for.

lines.caption: Folders are found relative to where you ran the command; with nothing before -T, the left pane gets that folder.
lines.say: Folders are found relative to where you ran the command; with nothing before dash capital T, the left pane gets that folder.

lines.caption: The window is new even when Open new windows as tabs is on.
With -t alone, split view is turned off, even if you always enable split view.
lines.say: With dash t alone, split view is turned off, even if you always enable split view.

lines.caption: Thunar normally selects the last tab opened, so the first tab is selected on purpose.
This table sums it up: -t a b -T c d fills both panes; -t a b fills only the left pane.
lines.say: This table sums it up: with both options, both panes fill; with dash t alone, only the left pane.

lines.caption: -T c alone puts the current folder on the left; -T with nothing after it is an error, and no window opens.
lines.say: Dash capital T with one folder puts the current folder on the left; with nothing after it, it's an error, and no window opens.

lines.caption: A missing folder gets the usual dialog, then the rest open; without these options nothing changes.
Two limits: thunar -T still exits with status 0, like every Thunar usage error, and remote locations aren't mounted.
lines.say: Two limits: the error still exits with status zero, like every Thunar usage error, and remote locations aren't mounted.

lines.caption: The PR changes three Thunar source files and adds a test, this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert this PR; nothing is stored in settings.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows issue 4's table, reuses Thunar's own new-window path, and Thunar's usual error dialog.
In this session's local run, not CI, it built with no new warnings, and the smoke test and all 10 tests passed.
lines.say: In this session's local run, not C I, it built with no new warnings, and the smoke test and all ten tests passed.

lines.caption: The new test ran the issue's example with no Thunar running, and stepped through both panes' tabs.
With Thunar running and new windows as tabs on, it still opened new windows, with and without the right pane.
The current folder filled the left pane; -T alone printed its error and opened nothing, but exits 0, so that check was dropped.
lines.say: The current folder filled the left pane; the option alone printed its error and opened nothing, but exits zero, so that check was dropped.

lines.caption: A missing folder got the error dialog and the rest opened, help lists both options, and the test took 18 seconds.
lines.say: A missing folder got the error dialog and the rest opened, help lists both options, and the test took eighteen seconds.

lines.caption: Not run: a file that isn't a folder, a remote location, and the visual audit of the screenshots.
A fresh review agent found six things before the first push: five were fixed, one kept on purpose.
Three were in the test script, and two in messages, like help with -T showing the error instead.
lines.say: Three were in the test script, and two in messages, like help with dash capital T showing the error instead.

lines.caption: Kept: -t alone turns split view off, because the issue asks for the left pane only.
lines.say: Kept: dash t alone turns split view off, because the issue asks for the left pane only.

lines.caption: CI's own review, at level high, hasn't run yet; it will report in its code review comment.
lines.say: C I's own review, at level high, hasn't run yet; it will report in its code review comment.

lines.caption: After the merge, try the options on your own desktop, with your own folders and settings.
The pull request, its checks and CI's comments are linked here.
lines.say: The pull request, its checks and C I's comments are linked here.

lines.caption: Part 3. What comes later: issue 41, a split option.
Issue 41 adds --split, which opens a new window with split view at a given percentage.
lines.say: Issue 41 adds a split option, which opens a new window with split view at a given percentage.

lines.caption: Whichever lands second makes -T windows open at that split, and -t alone open the right pane on the first tab.
lines.say: Whichever lands second makes these windows open at that split, and dash t alone open the right pane on the first tab.

lines.caption: Issue 41 is next: it adds the option, then wires it to this PR's tabs, as its own issue lists.
In short: one command now opens a new window with your chosen tabs in one or both panes, focus on the left.
